questionText:
Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM, average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors.

A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal places) to read the entire file from the disk is _________
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate Rotation Time and Average Rotational Latency.
Disk rotation speed = $6000\text{ RPM} = \frac{6000}{60} = 100\text{ rotations per second}$.
Time for 1 complete rotation = $\frac{1}{100}\text{ s} = 10\text{ ms}$.
Average Rotational Latency = $\frac{10\text{ ms}}{2} = 5\text{ ms}$.

Step 2: Calculate Sector Transfer Time.
Time to transfer 1 track (500 sectors) = $10\text{ ms}$.
Time to transfer 1 sector = $\frac{10\text{ ms}}{500} = 0.02\text{ ms}$.

Step 3: Calculate Time for 1 Randomly Located Sector.
Total time per sector = $\text{Seek Time} + \text{Rotational Latency} + \text{Transfer Time}$
Total time per sector = $5\text{ ms} + 5\text{ ms} + 0.02\text{ ms} = 10.02\text{ ms}$.

Step 4: Calculate Total Time to Read 3000 Sectors.
Because the 3000 sectors are located randomly, each sector read requires an independent seek, rotational latency, and transfer.
Total time = $3000 \times 10.02\text{ ms} = 30060\text{ ms} = 30.06\text{ seconds}$.

(Note: If transfer time is ignored, total time = $3000 \times (5 + 5)\text{ ms} = 30000\text{ ms} = 30.00\text{ seconds}$, which is also within the allowed range of $29.50$ to $30.50$ seconds.)
